newsitem.title: INDIA: India greets Bhutto's remarks with silence.
newsitem.headline: India greets Bhutto's remarks with silence.

text.p: India kept a studied silence on Friday after Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto said New Delhi was bent on deploying nuclear-capable missiles, and called recent elections in Kashmir a "sham".
The Foreign Ministry had no comment on Bhutto's remarks this week in New York. Newspapers all but ignored her comments.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) said that for the first time, India had decided not to exercise its right of reply after Bhutto addressed the U.N. General Assembly on Thursday.
"This was the first time India ignored the provocative Pakistani statements in the world body," PTI said.

PTI quoted Foreign Minister I.K. Gujral as telling the Foreign Policy Association in New York that "India would not respond to any provocative statement from Pakistan as a part of its effort to improve the relations".
Indian foreign policy analysts said Bhutto appeared to be trying to deflect attention from troubles at home, including sectarian strife, and that her comments did not reflect any mounting tensions.
In her speech, Bhutto proposed convening an ambitious international conference to resolve the long-festering Kashmir dispute with India and halt the danger of a nuclear arms race in South Asia.

The Pakistani leader said India sought last month to "divert world opinion by organising a sham election" in Jammu and Kashmir state. Pakistan rules over one third of the Kashmir region and has staked a claim to the rest.

Bhutto proposed that India and Pakistan, along with the five permanent members of the U.N. Security Council and other major powers such as Germany and Japan, convene a conference. Among the goals would be the resolution of the Kashmir dispute.
India's position since signing the Shimla Agreement with Pakistan in 1972 has been that the Kashmir dispute is strictly a bilateral matter.

The Indian Express quoted an Indian official in New York as saying "the attempt to drag in the members of the Security Council and countries like Germany and Japan was aimed at stalling India's attempts to gain membership of the Security Council".
PTI quoted Gujral as saying India was making concerted efforts to improve relations with its neighbours and expand trade and economic ties with other Asian nations.
Gujral was expected to address the U.N. General Assembly on Friday.
